notes:
Inbound from Y Combinator alum founders building an in-app AI assistant for B2B SaaS apps.

Quick summary:
- Primary product: lightweight in-app chat widget embedded in customer apps (SaaS).
- Traffic pattern: spiky daytime volume, avg 60 reqs/min during peak, expecting ~200 reqs/min in 6mo.
- Focus: streaming responses (token-by-token) so UX feels instantaneous; want server-sent events / websocket support.
- Target latency: 95th pct <200ms for first token on typical prompt lengths (short prompts ~60 tokens), subsequent tokens budgeted ~20-30ms per token.
- Cost sensitivity: startup budget, want predictable unit cost; interested in batching suggestions and quantized model options to lower spend.
- Model preference: open/llama-family preferred for costs, but flexible if Redwood hosted model offers better latency.
- Routing needs: single-region NA for now, optional fallback to smaller model when latency spike or quota hit.
- Security: SSO for admin console (SAML), audit logs for token usage, basic KMS integration later; no air-gapped requirement.

Conversation notes (call 2026-02-10 w/ Jordan + Aisha):
- "Streaming is must-have — product feels broken without it." (founder quote).
- Demo: used free hosted API credits, integrated websocket sample; observed jitter on long responses. AE suggested kv-prefix caching + smaller context windows.
- SE action: provide sample config for continuous batching + recommended model/quantization for 8GB GPU footprint.

POC asks:
- 2-week POC with 100k free tokens, streaming endpoints, and a short checklist for performance tuning.
- Provide sample throughput tests and a minimal tracing example to measure token latency (prefer OpenTelemetry hints).

Next steps (short):
- Provision POC tokens + enable streaming for their dev org (Jordan).
- SE to drop a sample config + perf tuning doc (Aisha) by 2026-02-19.
- Founder to route initial traffic and share perf logs; decision expected during March budget cycle.

Misc: referred to security FAQ in drive; Founder mentioned TOS concerns around customer data retention (needs simple retention controls).
